description.value: The Dinghy Dock Pub & Restaurant is Canada's only registered floating pub, moored off Protection Island in Nanaimo Harbour and reachable by passenger ferry, kayak, or private boat since 1989. The entirely floating structure offers panoramic views of Nanaimo Harbour and the surrounding Gulf Islands from every seat, indoors and out. Touring cyclists can ride to the ferry terminal at 151 Front Street in downtown Nanaimo and make the short crossing to enjoy classic pub fare and local Vancouver Island beers at this genuinely one-of-a-kind destination.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content is rich and corroborates OSM contact details (address, phone, email all match). The pub is Canada's only registered floating pub, moored off Protection Island and reachable only by ferry, kayak, or private boat — no road access exists, making conventional bike parking irrelevant and unmentioned on the site. No amenities specific to cyclists (bike parking, Wi-Fi, charging, etc.) are referenced anywhere in the website content or OSM tags, so all such fields are null. OSM opening hours (Mo-Su) conflict with the website (Fri/Mon open, Tue–Thu closed) — flagged as a concern but hours are excluded from output per rules.
concerns: OSM opening_hours tag (Mo-Su 11:30-21:00) conflicts with website, which shows Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday as closed — OSM data appears outdated.

Venue is a floating pub with no road access; cyclists must use the passenger ferry from 151 Front Street, Nanaimo. Bike transport on the ferry is not addressed on the website, which may affect usability for loaded touring cyclists.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operating, publicly accessible business confirmed by active website with 2026 menus and current hours. A notable destination stop for cyclists taking the Protection Island ferry from Nanaimo.
enrichment_extras.notes: Ferry dock for the Protection Island Ferry is at 151 Front Street, Nanaimo, BC V9R 5E2 — same phone and email as the pub. The pub website notes docking for vessels from kayak size up to 50-foot sail/power boats, so cyclists arriving by kayak can also tie up directly.
